tasks.title: Buy CT Pros domain + wire real website/email
tasks.notes: Domain needed for COMPANY_EMAIL, COMPANY_WEBSITE, MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS, GMAIL_OAUTH_FROM_ADDRESS placeholders. CT Pros LLC, Bridgeport CT.

prep.what: Purchase a domain for CT Pros LLC and wire it into the app's company identity + email config.
prep.understand: COMPANY_EMAIL='office@ctpros.example' (RFC-reserved non-deliverable) and COMPANY_WEBSITE='' are the two live placeholders. The new domain also drives MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS and GMAIL_OAUTH_FROM_ADDRESS — touch those wrong and QB OAuth callbacks and outbound email both break. Lesson from t72: after updating .env, rebuild `config:cache` AND restart the app container or OPcache serves the old cached config.
approach: Pick and buy the domain (ctprosllc.com, ctpros.pro, ctprospro.com — check availability) on Cloudflare Registrar or Namecheap. Use Cloudflare for DNS control.
Update staging .env: COMPANY_EMAIL='office@[domain]', COMPANY_WEBSITE='https://[domain]', MAIL_FROM_ADDRESS='office@[domain]', GMAIL_OAUTH_FROM_ADDRESS='office@[domain]'
Update the Gmail OAuth app in Google Cloud Console: add the new domain's authorized redirect URI for the QB callback and any mail-sending redirect.
SSH into staging, run `php artisan config:cache`, then restart the app container — verify via a test proposal PDF that the email and website render correctly.
resources: Google Cloud Console → OAuth 2.0 Clients (Gmail OAuth app for GMAIL_OAUTH_*)

tasks.title: Sandbox-validate QBVendorSync (Subcontractor→Vendor) live
tasks.notes: Mock-tested only. Validate adopt-by-DisplayName recovery (6240 error), Vendor1099 flag against real Intuit sandbox.

prep.what: Run QBVendorSync live against the Intuit sandbox to prove mock-tested Subcontractor→Vendor push actually works.
prep.understand: QBVendorSync is mock-tested against a MockHandler; it has never hit a real Intuit API. Key behaviors: adopt-by-DisplayName (finds existing vendor by name instead of creating a dup), 6240 error recovery, and Vendor1099 flag from `w9_on_file`. Set QUICKBOOKS_ENVIRONMENT=sandbox — never sandbox-test against production QB.
approach: Set QUICKBOOKS_ENVIRONMENT=sandbox in staging .env; rebuild config cache + restart app.
Create a test subcontractor in the app. Trigger sync via `/quickbooks/subcontractors/{id}/sync` or `php artisan quickbooks:sync`.
Open the Intuit Developer sandbox dashboard and verify: Vendor created with correct DisplayName + Vendor1099=true (if w9_on_file=true on the sub).
Test adopt-by-DisplayName: manually create a Vendor in the sandbox with the same name, then sync the subcontractor again — should ADOPT (no duplicate).
resources: QBVendorSyncTest.php (the mock test cases as a sequence guide)

tasks.title: Connect CT Pros’s own QuickBooks (fresh OAuth)
tasks.notes: Inherited tokens were HighTech's and never carried over. Run fresh OAuth against CT Pros's real QBO company.

prep.what: Run the QuickBooks OAuth flow to connect CT Pros's own QBO company, replacing HighTech's stale inherited tokens.
prep.understand: The QB integration is code-complete and mock-tested. Zero live QB calls have ever been made for CT Pros — `quickbooks_tokens` is empty or holds HighTech tokens. OAuth flow: Settings → Connect QuickBooks → Intuit redirect → authenticate → callback stores tokens encrypted in `quickbooks_tokens`. You need CT Pros's QBO credentials (get from Rafa).
approach: Log in to staging as admin (ADMIN_INITIAL_PASSWORD from staging .env). Navigate to Settings → QuickBooks.
Click 'Connect QuickBooks' — authenticate with CT Pros's QBO credentials (coordinate with Rafa if needed).
After callback: verify Settings shows 'Connected'. Check `quickbooks_tokens` table has a row with a non-null `access_token`.
Run `php artisan quickbooks:sync` — check logs for no auth errors. 401 means the token didn't save; re-run the OAuth flow.
resources: Staging app: Settings → QuickBooks (auth/quickbooks routes in routes/web.php)
CT Pros QBO admin credentials (from Rafa)

tasks.title: Sandbox-validate full QB round-trip against live Intuit
tasks.notes: All 6 entity mappings mock-tested only. Validate connect→estimate→invoice→paid + IPPLinkedTxn. Record docs/ artifact.

prep.what: End-to-end live test of all 6 QB entity syncs against the Intuit sandbox — Customer, Vendor, Item, Estimate, Invoice, Payment.
prep.understand: Every sync is mock-tested only. Critical: the IPPLinkedTxn that links Invoice back to Estimate — Intuit rejects malformed LinkedTxn silently and payment won't reconcile. Run with QUICKBOOKS_ENVIRONMENT=sandbox. This session produces the docs/ validation artifact required before go-live.
approach: Set QUICKBOOKS_ENVIRONMENT=sandbox in staging .env; connect sandbox QB via OAuth (Settings flow as t25).
Run full CRM flow: Create lead → build estimate → approve → verify auto deposit invoice pushed to QB with TxnStatus=Accepted and IPPLinkedTxn.
Simulate payment in sandbox (dev dashboard → Invoice → Receive Payment). Run `php artisan quickbooks:sync` — verify CRM shows payment received.
Document in docs/quickbooks-sandbox-validation.md: timestamp, each entity's QB ID, pass/fail for all 6 syncs, LinkedTxn verification.
resources: Intuit QBO API reference: Estimate, Invoice, Payment entities
docs/ folder for the validation artifact

tasks.title: Label lane v2: M3 vision for outlined-text firms + callout-vs-room filtering
tasks.notes: Live-text lane gets 0 labels on outlined-text PDFs (PDFTron firms). M3 tiles spike works but needs productizing + MINIMAX_AI key on VPS.

prep.what: Add an opt-in AI label endpoint using the MiniMax tiles lane for firms that outline all text, and filter out callout noise from real room names.
prep.understand: The free live-text lane works on standard PDFs (Holabird: 92/109 named) but fails on outlined-text firms (PDFTron outlines all text as paths — 55 live words found, zero room labels). The spike `docs/spike/run_labels_m3tiles.py` proves MiniMax M3 tiles work (~4.3 min/sheet, costs credits). Two sub-problems: (a) productize as an opt-in endpoint, (b) filter noise — Holabird shows UP arrows, FEC callouts, note paragraphs matching as room names.
approach: Read docs/spike/run_labels_m3tiles.py to understand the tile rendering + MiniMax vision call pattern. Identify what's reusable vs spike scaffolding.
Add route POST /sheets/{sheet}/labels-ai that triggers the M3 tiles lane as an opt-in action, emitting a §7a `metered_credits` event per the pattern in service/routes.py.
Wire MINIMAX_AI key to the VPS: add to /opt/takeoff-engine/.env; verify it reaches the service via config/settings.
Add callout-vs-room filtering: exclude stair markers (UP/DN), fire equipment (FEC), multi-word note paragraphs, and labels outside room boundary polygons. Check R13 docs for the full noise list.
resources: R13 docs for callout noise patterns

tasks.title: Assemblies-per-room → paint/drywall/flooring quantities + wall heights
tasks.notes: assemblies-lite scaffolded in engine/assemblies.py. Full version: room type → up to 8 assembly quantities. Last pillar before estimator-grade Excel.

prep.what: Build the full assemblies-per-room pipeline: room classification + geometry + wall height → up to 8 estimator quantities → Excel workbook.
prep.understand: The scaffold `engine/assemblies.py` exists from B1 (assemblies-lite). Full version: given a classified room + floor area + perimeter + `wall_height_ft` → compute quantities: wall paint SF (perimeter × height), ceiling paint SF (= floor area), flooring SF (= floor area), drywall SF (= wall SF), trim LF (= perimeter). These feed `build_sheet_takeoff` in service/worker.py and appear in the 5-tab Excel as new quantity rows. This is the last pillar before estimator-grade Excel.
approach: Open engine/assemblies.py — review the existing scaffold: what's wired vs placeholder. Understand what `build_sheet_takeoff` in service/worker.py currently calls.

Define the room classification → assembly mapping table: bedroom, bathroom, kitchen, corridor, living_room → their assembly sets (wall paint, ceiling paint, floor type, drywall, trim LF). Reference CSI MasterFormat Div 09 Finishes.
Wire `wall_height_ft`: read from the Measurement row (set via PATCH /room-table from t8); fall back to project default (e.g. 9 ft). Compute wall_sf = perimeter × wall_height_ft.

Plug assembly output into `build_sheet_takeoff` in service/worker.py: emit one assembly quantity row per assembly per room in the Excel. Run `pytest service/ -v` — verify 17+ existing tests still pass, then add a test for the new assembly rows.
resources: PATCH /room-table correction routes (t8 notes: wall_height_ft via model_fields_set)
